summary: alipclutch-baileys ships obfuscated network host in messages-send
details: This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library. In lib/Socket/messages-send.js (lines 425 and 436) the code reconstructs a network destination from a String.fromCharCode(...) decimal-ASCII array; the decoded value is the URL https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. Concealing the destination via character-code obfuscation rather than including it as a plain string is inconsistent with the upstream Baileys codebase, which uses no such obfuscation for its own endpoints. The presence of a hidden outbound host inside the messages-send code path — the module responsible for handling authenticated WhatsApp session traffic — is consistent with covert relay or exfiltration of session/message data through an author-controlled endpoint that the caller has not configured. The upstream Baileys project does not include this host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
